item.text: {"question_id":"6B.1","answer":"In 2023, Xi and the central government treated welfare as a genuine governing objective, but the supplied evidence does not establish it as the core purpose of government. Xi formally made people's interests, basic living needs, social security, basic public services, and common prosperity governing commitments (BATCH-0010-E005; BATCH-0018-E003). These commitments were accompanied by reported implementation and funding: fiscal measures supported employment, education, health care, pensions, vulnerable groups, rural development, and disaster recovery; a second 2023 assistance tranche directed funds to low-income and otherwise vulnerable groups; and official statistics recorded substantial education spending and social-insurance coverage (BATCH-0007-E001; BATCH-0011-E011; BATCH-0013-E006; BATCH-0026-E012). However, these are mainly official or administrative sources, and they do not independently establish delivery quality, equitable incidence, Xi-specific causation, or welfare priority relative to competing state objectives. In the same period, Xi-directed strategy emphasized industrial modernization and technological self-reliance, with socioeconomic targets described as subordinate to industrial policy so long as the economic baseline was maintained (BATCH-0001-E001; BATCH-0003-E003). China also devoted an estimated $296 billion to the military, up 6 percent in real terms and directed substantially toward PLA combat readiness, while a difficult-to-verify budget category covering diplomacy and external propaganda rose 12.2 percent (BATCH-0023-E012; BATCH-0021-E017). Independent human-rights assessments further documented intensified repression, social control, and severe abuses affecting Uyghurs, Tibetans, civil society, and political critics, including Xi's public endorsement of Xinjiang policies as a success (BATCH-0010-E017; BATCH-0010-E024; BATCH-0020-E007; BATCH-0022-E011). The best-supported conclusion is therefore that welfare was a real, funded, and partly implemented administrative objective under Xi in 2023, but its status as a core purpose was conditional and constrained by Party control, security, ideological, military, and strategic-industrial priorities. The evidence does not support claiming broad welfare gains were attributable to Xi personally beyond institutional attribution, nor does this one-year period establish durable
